paragraphs: Seder HaDorot takes Mati to be the name of a sage. Hyman says that the Penei Moshe’s reading of Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 7:9 is in fact more accurate: “Set aside what you said and teach it [with reference to consecrated offerings].”

notes.text: The supplied text reads מדרביך, “from your teacher”; earlier OCR has מדבריך, “from your words.” The phrase is retained with a tentative gloss, not treated as a newly established sage’s name.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Sanhedrin7 scalar at halakhah index8 contains אמרו ליה מטי תנה לקדשים. It is compatible with Hyman’s verbal interpretation, but does not itself inspect Penei Moshe or settle a competing proper-name reading. The supplied מדרביך (from your teacher) and OCR מדבריך (from your words) remain distinct. Seder HaDorot is the contextual סה״ד expansion; Hyman’s in-truth-more-correct judgment is attributed at full force. The gloss remains tentative; no mixed historical note is retired.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 880) and the consulted Penei Moshe both read מדבריך, “from your words,” where the supplied Hebrew has מדרביך, “from your teacher.” The Penei Moshe’s primary explanation treats the expression as an instruction to set aside the previous interpretation and apply the verse to consecrated offerings. He also offers another verbal gloss. The consulted Seder HaDorot entry takes Mati as a sage’s name and cites halakhah 11.
